sections.heading: B — Audience and scope
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience and scope

Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning the unattended-child law, safe backing, entering traffic from driveways and parking positions, roundabouts, choosing and changing lanes, keeping a safe speed and following interval, turns and curves, overtaking and passing, passing parked cars, stopping in traffic, use of brakes and downshifting in plain English.

Prerequisites: the right-of-way, signal and no-passing laws of the traffic laws section, which these techniques apply on the road.

Scope note: the unattended-child law, safe backing, entering traffic from driveways and parking positions, roundabouts, choosing and changing lanes, keeping pace and the two-second interval, turns and curves, overtaking and passing with its abort rule, passing parked cars, stopping in traffic, the physics and use of brakes, emergency braking and downshifting. Parking, signals and weather follow in the next section.

Recall emphasis: the two-second count, the one-hundred-foot signal and the child rule are practiced as recall items, while passing and lane-change decisions feed the dedicated scene-decision surface declared in part C.

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the the unattended-child law, safe backing, entering traffic from driveways and parking positions, roundabouts, choosing and changing lanes, keeping a safe speed and following interval, turns and curves, overtaking and passing, passing parked cars, stopping in traffic, use of brakes and downshifting rules on pages 64–70 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
